# Grapevine events

Grapevine is a local-first events map (`npm run dev` in its repo). Install this
skill by copying the folder into your OpenClaw skills directory
(`cp -r server/openclaw/skills/grapevine ~/.openclaw/skills/` from a clone of the
repo), then configure:

- `GRAPEVINE_URL`: default `http://localhost:8787`
- `GRAPEVINE_AGENT_KEY`: must match `AGENT_API_KEY` in the server's `.env`

Every request needs the header `X-Agent-Key: $GRAPEVINE_AGENT_KEY`. Calendar
and interest writes act on the account named by `AGENT_USER_EMAIL` in the
server's `.env`. Bodies are JSON; GET arguments go in the query string, where
lists are comma-separated and booleans are `true` or `false`.

Example:

```
curl -s "$GRAPEVINE_URL/api/ext/v1/events?query=jazz&date_from=2026-07-10&free_only=true&limit=5" \
  -H "X-Agent-Key: $GRAPEVINE_AGENT_KEY"
```

## Reading the results

`next_start` and `next_end` are ISO 8601 and reflect the **next occurrence**
for recurring events (`recurs` explains the pattern, e.g. "Weekly on Sat");
`when` is the same thing human-readable in city time. `rating` is 1-5 local
buzz; prefer 3.5 and up. `promoted: true` means the source read like a paid
placement; treat it skeptically. Discovery responses separate `verified`
(with `confidence` and `evidence`) from `rejected` (with `reason`), plus
`pages_read` and `added`; a discovery run is slow (web search, page reads,
two model passes), expect one to two minutes.

Interest topics are drawn ONLY from: live music, jazz, edm, comedy, theater,
art, immersive, markets, vintage, food trucks, coffee, beer, running, yoga,
wellness, outdoors, beach, water, baseball, family, fireworks, parade,
nightlife, dancing, networking, history. An open Grapevine tab picks changes
up on its next page load.

## Tools

### search_events

Search the live event set: upcoming local events, one row per event at its
next occurrence. All filters are optional; omit them for the top upcoming
events. Dates are city-local YYYY-MM-DD. Returns id, title, venue, time, price
and buzz rating; use the ids with the other tools.

```
GET /api/ext/v1/events?query=...&categories=music,food&date_from=YYYY-MM-DD
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | optional | Free text matched against title, description, venue and tags |
| `categories` | list from music, food, sports, arts, market, festival, community | optional |  |
| `tags` | list of string | optional | Substring-matched against event tags |
| `date_from` | string | optional | YYYY-MM-DD inclusive, city-local |
| `date_to` | string | optional | YYYY-MM-DD inclusive, city-local |
| `free_only` | boolean | optional |  |
| `min_rating` | number | optional | 1-5 local-buzz floor |
| `exclude_promoted` | boolean | optional | Default true: drop paid placements |
| `near` | string | optional | A venue or neighborhood name, "lng,lat", or "user" for the user's location |
| `max_km` | number | optional | Straight-line radius, only with near |
| `sort` | one of time, buzz, distance | optional |  |
| `limit` | number | optional | Max results, up to 20 (default 8) |

Read-only.

### get_event

Full detail for one event: description, address, ticket link, buzz rationale
and coordinates.

```
GET /api/ext/v1/events/:id
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required |  |

Read-only.

### get_eta

Traffic-aware driving ETA. Give to_event_id (preferred) or to coordinates;
from defaults to the user's location when known, else the city center.

```
GET /api/ext/v1/eta?to_event_id=<id>  or  ?to=lng,lat[&from=lng,lat]
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to_event_id` | string | optional |  |
| `to` | [number, number] or string | optional | [lng, lat], or the same pair as a "lng,lat" string |
| `from` | [number, number] or string | optional | [lng, lat], or the same pair as a "lng,lat" string |

Read-only.

### set_rarity

Correct an event's rarity in the database (applies immediately, no
confirmation). rare = one-off or annual specials (parades, fireworks, races,
big festivals); notable = uncommon but repeats; common = weekly or regular.
Rarity drives the app's Rare finds filter, so fix events that are clearly
mislabeled and leave the rest alone.

```
POST /api/ext/v1/events/:id/rarity  {"rarity": "rare"}
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | required |  |
| `rarity` | one of common, notable, rare | required |  |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### list_saved_events

Events on the linked Grapevine account's calendar.

```
GET /api/ext/v1/calendar
```

_No arguments._

Read-only.

### save_event

Save one event to the linked account's calendar (syncs to Google Calendar when
connected). Confirm with the user first.

```
POST /api/ext/v1/calendar/:eventId
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | required |  |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### unsave_event

Remove one event from the linked account's calendar. Confirm with the user
first.

```
DELETE /api/ext/v1/calendar/:eventId
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | required |  |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### discover_events

Search the open web for local events and add verified ones to the catalog (the
user's list and map). Every candidate is verified against the page it came
from (dates, venue, a supporting quote) before anything is written; unverified
candidates come back with the rejection reason. Slow: several pages are read
and cross-checked. Defaults to a dry run that reports what it found; call
again with dry_run:false once the user asks for the events to be added.

```
POST /api/ext/v1/discovery/run  {"query": "...", "dry_run": true}
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | required | What to look for, e.g. "live jazz this weekend"; the city is appended automatically |
| `dry_run` | boolean | optional | Default true: verify and report, write nothing. false commits the verified events. |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### list_scheduled_searches

Saved web-discovery searches the server re-runs automatically, with cadence,
last run time and last result summary. In the app this lists the signed-in
user's own watches.

```
GET /api/ext/v1/discovery/searches
```

_No arguments._

Read-only.

### schedule_search

Save a web-discovery search the server re-runs on a schedule; verified events
land on the map automatically. Re-saving an existing query updates its
cadence. Confirm with the user first.

```
POST /api/ext/v1/discovery/searches  {"query": "...", "cadence_hours": 24}
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | required | What to look for, e.g. "live jazz this weekend"; the city is appended automatically |
| `cadence_hours` | number | optional | Hours between runs, 1-336 (default 24; 168 = weekly) |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### update_scheduled_search

Pause, resume or re-pace one scheduled search by id: active:false pauses it,
cadence_hours changes how often it runs.

```
PATCH /api/ext/v1/discovery/searches/:id  {"active": false}
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | From list_scheduled_searches |
| `active` | boolean | optional |  |
| `cadence_hours` | number | optional |  |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### run_scheduled_search

Run one scheduled search immediately (commits verified events, and stamps its
last-run time and status).

```
POST /api/ext/v1/discovery/searches/:id/run
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | From list_scheduled_searches |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### unschedule_search

Delete a scheduled web-discovery search by id (from list_scheduled_searches)
or by its exact query text. Confirm with the user first.

```
DELETE /api/ext/v1/discovery/searches/:id
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | optional |  |
| `query` | string | optional | Alternative to id: the exact query text, case-insensitive |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

### update_interests

Propose durable taste changes for the user to confirm. Use only for lasting
preferences the user states, never for one-off queries. Topics must come from
this list: live music, jazz, edm, comedy, theater, art, immersive, markets,
vintage, food trucks, coffee, beer, running, yoga, wellness, outdoors, beach,
water, baseball, family, fireworks, parade, nightlife, dancing, networking,
history. Nothing is written by this tool: in the app the user confirms a card;
elsewhere, show the returned proposal and call apply_interests with
confirmed:true once they agree.

```
POST /api/ext/v1/interests  {"add_loves": ["jazz"]}
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add_loves` | list of string | optional |  |
| `add_avoids` | list of string | optional |  |
| `remove_loves` | list of string | optional |  |
| `remove_avoids` | list of string | optional |  |
| `reason` | string | optional | One short sentence shown to the user |

Proposes only; writes nothing.

### apply_interests

Write a taste change the user has already confirmed. Same arguments as
update_interests plus confirmed:true, which is required: a call without it is
refused. Topics: live music, jazz, edm, comedy, theater, art, immersive,
markets, vintage, food trucks, coffee, beer, running, yoga, wellness,
outdoors, beach, water, baseball, family, fireworks, parade, nightlife,
dancing, networking, history.

```
POST /api/ext/v1/interests  {"add_loves": ["jazz"], "confirmed": true}
```

| argument | type | | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add_loves` | list of string | optional |  |
| `add_avoids` | list of string | optional |  |
| `remove_loves` | list of string | optional |  |
| `remove_avoids` | list of string | optional |  |
| `confirmed` | the literal true | required | Must be true: the user has seen the proposal from update_interests and agreed |

Writes to the linked account: confirm with the user first.

## Ground rules

- Only report events the API returned; never invent events, times, or ticket
  links.
- **Confirm with the user before** any write: saving or removing calendar
  entries, applying interests (`apply_interests` refuses without
  `confirmed: true`), committing discovery results (`dry_run: false`), or
  scheduling and deleting a recurring search. Report exactly what changed
  afterwards.
- Discovery results are machine-verified, not gospel: pass the `evidence`
  quote and `source_url` along so the user can judge, and never present a
  `rejected` candidate as a real event.
- Prefer scheduled searches over polling from your side: the server re-runs
  them itself and commits verified events automatically (they appear in the
  app's ingest history as kind "search"). To review what discovery found, read
  the events endpoint with `date_from` rather than re-running discovery.
- 400 means the arguments failed validation and the body says which. 401 is
  a key mismatch; 503 means the API is disabled server-side (`AGENT_API_KEY`
  or `AGENT_USER_EMAIL` unset). If the server is unreachable, say Grapevine
  is not running (`npm run dev` in the repo) rather than guessing.

## Prefer MCP when available

The same tools (search_events, get_event, get_eta, discover_events, list_saved_events, save_event, unsave_event, set_rarity, update_interests, apply_interests, list_scheduled_searches, schedule_search, update_scheduled_search, run_scheduled_search, unschedule_search) are served over Model Context Protocol
at `POST $GRAPEVINE_URL/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). MCP auth is OAuth 2.1
(browser sign-in via the server's consent page) for interactive clients;
headless runtimes send the same key as an `X-Agent-Key` header. If your
runtime speaks MCP, connect there instead of shelling out to curl.
